summary: Abridgment of 'Berlin (1858-1859)' that keeps all seven verbatim excerpts, the ironic third-person retrospective voice, and the cross-chapter hooks: Marx, the dynamo, the ghost of the Civil Law, the accidental gain, Gotterdammerung, the Sumner 'worshipper' and the Thuringen tramp.
acceptable_changes: Dropped Captain Judkins, G. P. R. James, the Adelphi coffee-room and the Charles the First tower. They are optional and not needed later.
Shortened the London catalogue to Fleet Street/Johnson, the yellow chariots and the insolent Exchange and Bank. Kept the eighteenth-century verdict.
Compressed the Antwerp band and peasants to one image. Cut Ostade, Teniers and Alva.
Reduced the regent and Bismarck to one sentence. Cut the Thiergarten tramps, the food details and the description of the Gymnasium's class background.
Cut the Vienna dancing comparison, the 'thought himself Germanized' passage, and the detail on the German theatre and opera.
Replaced the paragraph-5 opening with the short source-backed bridge 'He did notice one peculiarity of London worth remembering'. Replaced 'Baron Osy' with 'the steamer'.
risks: Total length is estimated near the 2200 target, but no count tool was available.
Sumner's quote was restructured slightly, placing 'as he said with his grand air of mastery' before the line. The speech wording itself is from the source.
review_focus: The transition from London to 'Education went backward' and Antwerp. Confirm the fifty-years retrospect reads as later judgment.
The poodle and cabman echo after Sumner's line.
The Descent from the Cross setup before 'kneeling at the foot of the Cross'.
